style: Disciplined 4-2-3-1 under Miroslav Koubek built on a compact low block and quick transitions. Exceptional aerial and set-piece threat (led all European nations with eight set-piece goals in qualifying), spearheaded by the towering Schick and Soucek.
recent_form: Reached the finals through UEFA qualifying. Opened the World Cup with a 2-1 defeat to South Korea in Group A, with South Africa and Mexico still to come.

key_players.name: Patrik Schick
key_players.note: Bayer Leverkusen marksman and Czechia's go-to goalscorer; lethal in the air and the focal point of attacks.

key_players.name: Tomas Soucek
key_players.note: West Ham midfielder providing the spine; huge aerial threat on set pieces at both ends.

key_players.name: Ladislav Krejci
key_players.note: Captains the side and organizes the back line; comfortable bringing the ball out.

key_players.name: Robin Hranac
key_players.note: Hoffenheim defender; part of a compact central defensive unit.

key_players.name: Matej Kovar
key_players.note: First-choice keeper anchoring the low block.

key_players.name: Tomas Holes
key_players.note: Versatile, hard-working presence ahead of the defence.

historical_news: Qualified for the 2026 World Cup via the UEFA route under coach Miroslav Koubek.
Led all European nations with eight set-piece goals during qualifying, underlining their dead-ball strength.
Opened the tournament with a 2-1 loss to South Korea in Group A.
Drawn in Group A alongside Mexico, South Korea and South Africa.
Squad heavily reliant on the Schick-Soucek axis after the gradual departure of the previous golden generation.

media_sentiment.label: neutral
media_sentiment.summary: Measured expectations in Czech media: respected for organization and set-piece prowess but seen as lacking star depth; the opening loss to South Korea raised pressure to recover against South Africa and Mexico.
